analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers is a debt-free, promoter-heavy (74.67%) IT services micro-cap with a 28% revenue CAGR and 39% net profit CAGR over 5 years, trading at a modest 8.91x P/E. However, FY25 shows worrying deceleration (revenue +2%, operating income -12%), which fails my core requirement of sustained multi-year growth runway.
key_strengths: Strong compounding: Revenue 5Y CAGR 28.1%, Net Profit CAGR 39.1%, FCF positive all 5 years
Pristine balance sheet: zero borrowings since FY24, ROCE 26.5%, ROE 20%
Founder-aligned: 74.67% promoter holding, recent IPO raised ~₹64 Cr equity
key_risks: FY25 revenue growth collapsed to ~2% and operating income contracted 12% YoY
Sub-scale (₹100 Cr revenue) digital services firm with no disclosed R&D or proprietary IP
Global discretionary IT-spend cycle plus AI-driven commoditization of staff-augmentation work
red_flags: FY25 operating margin compression and top-line stall after years of 20%+ growth
Huge ₹77 Cr investing outflow in FY25 post-IPO — deployment thesis unclear
Negligible FII (0.73%) and DII (4.60%) participation signals limited institutional scrutiny
analysis.detailed_analysis: From my growth-investing lens, CapitalNumbers displays several fingerprints I look for in an emerging compounder: a founder-led, debt-free business with 28% revenue CAGR, expanding equity, and ROCE above 25%. The P/E of 8.91 is cheap for this growth profile and signals the market has not yet recognized the franchise — or, more likely, is pricing in the FY25 slowdown. Scuttlebutt on Indian digital consulting peers suggests demand softness across global discretionary IT spend, so the deceleration may be cyclical rather than structural.\n\nThat said, my checklist raises red flags. Revenue growth collapsing from ~28% to ~2% in a single year fails Question #1 (sufficient market potential) until proven otherwise, and with no disclosed R&D intensity, Questions #2 and #3 are unanswered. This is a sub-scale services firm, not a product innovator, so the quality-of-growth bar is lower than I prefer. I would hold, watch two more quarters for re-acceleration and margin recovery, and size up only if FY26 H1 confirms >20% growth resumption.
